DecSummary: The worker injured the right shoulder in 1984 while employed as a labourer and was awarded an 8% permanent partial disability benefit. The worker underwent surgery and participated in vocational rehabilitation services (VR) from 1987 to 1989 but was unsuccessful in finding suitable work. VR services were closed in December 1989 due to lack of communication, though the worker reported self-employment and no interference from the injury in 1990. The worker later returned to full-time work in 1991 and again with the employer in 2000 until retirement in 2024.

DecSummary: The worker suffered a back injury on September 22, 2017, diagnosed as lumbar sprain/strain with L5 nerve root syndrome, and was granted entitlement and a 7% non-economic loss (NEL) award. The worker returned to modified duties but was laid off in October 2017 and experienced further periods off work due to flare-ups and a second head injury in 2018. The issues under appeal were entitlement to Chronic Pain Disability (CPD) benefits or ongoing psychotraumatic disability, suitability of modified work offered, and LOE benefits entitlement from October 16, 2018.

DecSummary: The worker sustained permanent injuries to her neck, upper and lower back, and left eye traumatic macular edema/paracentral scotoma due to an MVA while traveling in a taxi for work. She received a 22% Non-Economic Loss (NEL) award for these injuries. The worker's entitlement was expanded to include psychotraumatic disability. Psychological treatments, including driver desensitization therapy, were approved by the WSIB. The employer appealed an ARO decision which granted 25% SIEF relief.

DecSummary: The worker suffered a right knee injury from a slip and fall at work on January 25, 2023, initially accepted as a contusion, joint effusion, and strain, with subsequent allowance for arthritis worsening and permanent impairment. The worker was granted secondary entitlement for psychotraumatic disability with permanent impairment. This appeal concerned the worker's entitlement to benefits for a right knee intramedullary lesion and the suitability of an accommodated pre-injury job at the time of a layoff.

DecSummary: The worker, employed as a utility locator since 2016, developed left foot and toe pain on September 7, 2021, attributed to his walking duties. The WSIB initially denied entitlement for plantar fasciitis, osteoarthritis (OA) in the left second metatarsophalangeal joint, and metatarsalgia, concluding these were not caused by work duties. The denial was upheld on appeal by the ARO in 2022.
